papers.title: Incidence of Colorectal Cancer After Endoscopic Mucosal Resection: A Multicenter Electronic Health Record Cohort Study
papers.authors: Eldesouki M, Elfert K, Ibrahim E, Youssef M, Shaukat A, Thakkar S
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) is widely used for large and complex colorectal lesions and offers a less invasive alternative to surgery. Although adenoma recurrence after EMR has been described in procedural cohorts, real-world estimates of subsequent colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnoses after EMR across multicenter electronic health record (EHR) systems remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Patients aged 40 years or older who underwent colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy with EMR between January 1, 2016 and January 1, 2017 were included. Patients with Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, familial adenomatous polyposis, or CRC recorded on or before the index EMR date were excluded. The primary outcome was incident CRC, defined by ICD-10-CM codes C18, C19, and C20, assessed from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2021 after a one-year washout period. Incidence rates are reported per 1,000 person-years with exact Poisson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A sensitivity analysis was restricted to patients aged 50-75 years at index EMR.
RESULTS: Among 3,081 eligible patients, the mean age was 62.9 ± 8.89 years and 52% were female; 2,735 were at risk at the start of follow-up. Twenty-two incident CRC diagnoses occurred over 10,187.8 person-years, an incidence of 2.16 per 1,000 person-years (95% CI, 1.35-3.27). Each calendar year contained 10 or fewer events, so annual rates could not be estimated. Incidence was 2.54 (95% CI, 1.31-4.44) in males and 1.83 (95% CI, 0.88-3.36) in females. In the 50-75-year sensitivity cohort, 19 events occurred over 8,894.8 person-years (2.14 per 1,000 person-years; 95% CI, 1.29-3.34). During years 1-5 after index EMR, repeat EMR occurred in 119 patients (3.9%), colorectal surgery in 28 (0.9%), and subsequent colorectal polyp diagnoses in 1,321 (42.9%); no ESD procedures were identified.
CONCLUSION: CRC diagnoses after EMR were uncommon in this multicenter EHR cohort, occurring at about 2 per 1,000 person-years. Event counts were too small to estimate annual trends or to compare incidence reliably across race and ethnicity groups. Studies linking EHR data to endoscopy and pathology reports are needed to identify preventable cancers after EMR.

papers.title: Colonoscopy-based Clostridioides difficile screening for inflammatory bowel disease patients
papers.authors: Allegretti J, Carlin A, McClure E, Delaney M, Bry L
papers.abstract: Patients with IBD have an increased risk for Clostridioides difficile infection, and the significance of asymptomatic colonization is poorly understood. Overlapping symptoms often complicate diagnosis, and there is a lack of validated screening methods. Colonic wash aspirates collected during routine colonoscopies may offer a convenient screening option. We aimed to evaluate culture methods for detecting C. difficile colonization in IBD patients using colonic wash samples. Patients with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis undergoing outpatient colonoscopy were enrolled. Clinical characteristics, IBD activity indices, and endoscopic scores were recorded. Colonic wash aspirates were centrifuged and cultured on selective CHROMID® media with and without broth enrichment. Isolates were confirmed by Gram stain and MALDI-TOF. PCR/qPCR identified tcdB gene carriage. Whole-genome sequencing was performed on selected isolates, and associations between clinical factors and colonization were assessed. Of the 121 patients enrolled, 10.7% (13/121) were colonized. Crohn's patients were colonized more frequently than ulcerative colitis patients (13.3% CD, 8.2% UC). Among colonized patients, 53.8% (7/13) had C. difficile with detectable tcdB. Enrichment increased detection compared to direct plating. No clinical predictors of colonization were identified, but wash samples yielded sufficient DNA for sequencing with comparable depth to whole stool. Colonoscopy wash aspirates allow for the detection of asymptomatic C. difficile colonization in IBD. This screening method may provide a useful tool for investigating the prevalence, persistence, and clinical significance of C. difficile colonization in IBD and for informing future studies of CDI prevention.

papers.title: ECCO Topical Review: Inflammatory Bowel Disease-Like Patterns of Drug Colitis with Practical Guidance and a Focus on Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Induced Enterocolitis
papers.authors: Verstockt B, Dragoni G, van Schaik F, Nunes P, Burisch J, Carbonnel F
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-induced enterocolitis (DIC) consists of a heterogeneous group of gastrointestinal inflammatory disorders with clinical, endoscopic, and histological features that often overlap with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Given the increasing recognition of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-induced enterocolitis and the lack of standardized management algorithms, the European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation (ECCO) convened a multidisciplinary panel to review DIC, with a particular focus on ICI-induced disease.
METHODS: Gastroenterologists, histopathologists, and oncologists systematically reviewed the literature using Medline, PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus. Evidence was synthesized into ECCO Current Practice Positions addressing diagnostic principles, histopathological patterns, therapeutic strategies, and ICI-specific considerations. Statements were refined and approved through structured consensus.
RESULTS: Twenty-three practice positions were agreed upon. DIC may present with diverse histological patterns, including IBD-like/chronic enterocolitis, acute enterocolitis, microscopic colitis, ischemic-type injury, and mixed features, none of which are pathognomonic. Close clinicopathological collaboration is therefore essential. In suspected ICI-induced enterocolitis, assessment should include Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events-based grading, stool testing for pathogens, fecal calprotectin, endoscopy with biopsies, and imaging when indicated. Corticosteroids remain first-line therapy, while mild or microscopic disease may respond to budesonide or beclomethasone. Corticosteroid-refractory or corticosteroid-dependent disease should prompt early escalation to infliximab or vedolizumab. Surgery is reserved for refractory or complicated cases. Rechallenge with ICIs may be considered following multidisciplinary evaluation.
CONCLUSION: DIC represents a diagnostically complex spectrum of disorders that require integrated multidisciplinary evaluation. These ECCO Current Practice Positions provide a practical framework for diagnostic work-up and treatment, particularly for ICI-induced enterocolitis.

papers.title: Roles of protein crotonylation in tumors: regulatory mechanisms and therapeutic potential
papers.authors: Liang Y, Liu Q, Yang C, Xun Y, Liu Y, Shen Y
papers.abstract: Lysine crotonylation(Kcr), an important protein post-translational modification, establishes a connection between cellular metabolism and epigenetic regulation. This modification utilizes crotonyl-CoA as a donor and is co-regulated by "writers", "erasers" and "readers". Furthermore, it participates in key biological processes including gene transcription, metabolic reprogramming, DNA damage repair, and remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Recent studies have demonstrated that crotonylation is dysregulated in various malignant tumors, including breast cancer, colorectal cancer, liver cancer, lung cancer, and glioma. It drives tumor proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and drug resistance by influencing metabolic enzyme activity, chromatin status, DNA repair efficiency, and immune signaling pathways. Lysine crotonylation demonstrates significant environmental-dependence across different cancers; Not only can it promote the malignant phenotype of tumor cells, but it can also potentiate the response to immunotherapy under specific metabolic conditions. Preclinical studies have explored therapeutic strategies targeting tumor crotonylation, including metabolic interventions, enzymatic regulation, and combination immunotherapy; however, these approaches remain investigational and have not been clinically validated. This narrative review summarizes the molecular mechanisms, biological functions, and current advances of crotonylation in diverse malignancies, and highlights unresolved questions and emerging therapeutic hypotheses.

papers.title: B cell/adipocyte crosstalk amplifies MCP-1 secretion, M2-like macrophage accumulation, and polarization in gut-associated, inflamed adipose tissue
papers.authors: Goess M, Heinze J, Hofmann J, Buck A, Gadjalova I, Weber M
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: During Crohn's disease (CD), hyperplasia of the mesenteric white adipose tissue (WAT), called creeping fat (CrF), is associated with the accumulation of immune cells. Here we investigated the impact of B cell/adipocyte crosstalk on immune cell recruitment and inflammation within inflammatory bowel disease-related adipose tissue.
METHODS: We used flow cytometry and in vitro 3D culture systems of biopsies from CrF of CD patients as well as a mouse model of intestinal inflammation, in vitro co-cultures, mass spectrometry, and single-cell RNA sequencing to evaluate the impact of B cell/adipocyte interplay on monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) production and macrophage polarization.
RESULTS: Employing primary human and mouse 3D adipocyte cultures, we observed that adipocytes from CD patients displayed a persistent inflammatory phenotype even after prolonged time in culture, a cytokine secretion profile also recapitulated via lipopolysaccharide stimulation. Analyzing CrF of CD patients as well as WAT of a mouse model of intestinal inflammation, we found an accumulation of B cells. B cell/adipocyte co-cultures led to elevated secretion of MCP-1 by primary adipocytes, facilitating macrophage migration. Consequently, co-transfer of B cells with T cells increased T cell activation and M2-like macrophage accumulation in inflamed mouse WAT. Mass spectrometry and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses suggested that the B cell/adipocyte crosstalk establishes a microenvironment that may promote M2-like macrophage polarization.
CONCLUSION: B cell/adipocyte interactions in CD-associated inflamed adipose tissue increase MCP-1 and lactate, promoting recruitment and M2-like polarization of macrophages, likely amplifying local WAT inflammation.

papers.title: Helicobacter pylori and colorectal neoplasia with emphasis on microbial mechanisms and causal evidence
papers.journal_full: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is associated with colorectal neoplasia in many observational studies, but a causal relationship and a preventive effect of eradication remain unestablished. This narrative review integrates clinical, microbial, experimental, and treatment evidence using four questions: which infection phenotype was measured, whether exposure preceded the colorectal outcome, whether a proposed intermediate was experimentally perturbed, and whether a defined intervention changed that outcome. Positive observational syntheses contrast with weaker or inconsistent prospective serological and genetic findings. Residual confounding, including socioeconomic and lifestyle differences, and non-equivalent exposure measurements limit causal interpretation. Gastric atrophy, endocrine changes, microbial remodeling, metabolites, and immune responses provide candidate links, but no complete infection-to-neoplasia sequence has been demonstrated in humans. Microbiota-dependent tumor promotion in genetically susceptible mice provides experimental support within that setting, whereas reduced tumor formation in an inflammation-driven model limits generalization. Neither model reproduces the duration and heterogeneity of human infection. Eradication findings depend on comparator selection, sufficient latency, and separation of randomized treatment assignment from successful clearance. A comparative appraisal links each proposed mechanism to its strongest available evidence, unresolved human causal link, and required validation. Infection status alone is not established as a basis for changing colorectal screening or claiming colorectal cancer prevention through eradication. Longitudinal human sampling, targeted tests of candidate intermediates, and long-term intervention analyses with explicit treatment comparisons are needed to establish clinical relevance.

papers.title: From Radical Resection to Organ Preservation in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Narrative Review of Risk-Adapted Management
papers.authors: Cetin B, Karaman I, Erdem D, Kaya E, Okumus N
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesise evidence informing risk-adapted treatment and organ preservation in locally advanced rectal cancer.
METHODS: This narrative review used targeted English-language searches of PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through 31 March 2026, supplemented by targeted source verification in September 2026.
RESULTS: Magnetic resonance imaging, mismatch repair status, recurrence risk, and patient preferences inform treatment selection. Total neoadjuvant therapy is established for higher-risk mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable disease. Chemoradiation followed by consolidation chemotherapy can improve organ-preservation probability compared with induction sequencing, without a demonstrated disease-free survival advantage. Selected lower-risk surgical candidates may receive chemotherapy with selective chemoradiation. Both short-course radiotherapy and long-course chemoradiation remain evidence-based options; the long-term locoregional failure signal in RAPIDO cannot be attributed to fractionation alone. Watch-and-wait requires multimodal confirmation of clinical complete response, intensive surveillance, and access to salvage surgery; oncological equivalence to immediate resection is unproven. Prospective dostarlimab data support non-operative management in selected mismatch repair-deficient rectal cancers, while long-term durability requires further evaluation.
CONCLUSION: Management should integrate tumour anatomy, biology, treatment response, and patient priorities. Organ preservation requires careful selection and structured follow-up, with treatment intensity individualised rather than applied uniformly.

papers.title: Preoperative classification of histopathological growth patterns in colorectal liver metastases using prospective 18 F-FDG PET/CT
papers.authors: Jonsson J, Ling A, Axelsson J, Lundin M, Vermeulen P, Riklund K
papers.abstract: Colorectal liver metastases (CLM) exhibit distinct histopathological growth patterns (HGPs) at the metastasis-liver interface, clinically relevant for prognosis and potential predictive value. This study investigates the feasibility of using Fluorine-18 Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) to preoperatively classify HGPs in CLM and secondly investigate PET parameters as prognostic markers for overall survival (OS). In a prospective study at Umeå University Hospital (June 2013-December 2017), 78 patients with resectable CLM underwent contrast-enhanced liver MRI and 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging. HGP classification was performed on tissue sections according to 2017 international guidelines. PET features (SUVmean [standardised uptake value], SUVmax, metabolic tumour volume [MTV] and first-order texture metrics) were analysed to distinguish encapsulating (eHGP) from replacement (rHGP) patterns. In pretreated patients, multivariate logistic regression including both metabolic and texture parameters identified significant associations for parameters from the fixed level threshold algorithm (VuePoint Sharp IR) with small odds ratios. Overall, PET parameters showed limited ability to discriminate between eHGP and rHGP. OS was superior with eHGP versus rHGP (log-rank p = 0.045). In chemonaïve patients, SUV-based metrics showed unadjusted exploratory associations with OS after liver surgery, varying by reconstruction/delineation and were not significant after correction for multiple testing. FDG-PET-derived parameters were not reliably associated with HGP and did not support non-invasive HGP prediction in this cohort. eHGP was associated with superior survival, underscoring the value of HGP assessment for prognostication while alternative non-invasive biomarkers remain to be identified.

papers.title: HtrA3 Promotes Malignant Progression of Colorectal Cancer and Is Associated With PI3K-AKT-FOXO1 Signaling
papers.authors: Zheng J, Ren S, Huang X, Ren S, Chen J, Wang D
papers.abstract: High-temperature requirement protease A3 (HtrA3) has been implicated in the progression of various carcinomas through tissue-specific mechanisms; however, its precise role in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. We initially identified the upregulation of HtrA3 in CRC tissues through Isobaric Tags for Relative and Absolute Quantitation (iTRAQ) proteomics, which was consistent with the analysis of the CPTAC dataset. Our research further confirmed that HtrA3 is significantly upregulated in CRC tissues and associated with reduced overall survival. Functional assays showed that HtrA3 overexpression enhanced CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while HtrA3 knockdown yielded opposite effects. In HtrA3-overexpressing HCT116 cells, increased phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and FOXO1 was observed, which was reduced upon treatment with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Conversely, in HtrA3-knockdown SW480 cells, these phosphorylation levels declined but were restored with the PI3K activator 740Y-P. In vivo, HtrA3 overexpression accelerated xenograft tumor growth. These findings suggest that HtrA3 promotes CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, potentially involving PI3K-AKT-FOXO1 signaling, and support further investigation of HtrA3 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in CRC.

papers.title: Digital health support for colorectal cancer patients: a patient centred approach
papers.journal_full: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.authors: Lee H, Mao B, Tucker J, Harrison A, Chamberlain R, Juszczyk K
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Colorectal cancer patients frequently report unmet information across physical, psychological, and social domains. Technology offers a promising solution for delivering tailored support. This qualitative study aims to identify and explore the information needs of colorectal cancer patients from diagnosis through surveillance and to understand their preferred digital delivery methods for clinical and supportive content. It represents the initial phase of a broader project to co-design a digital platform to support colorectal cancer patients.
METHODS: A qualitative research design with purposive sample of newly diagnosed colorectal cancer patients and colorectal cancer survivors attending outpatient review between May and August 2024. Open-ended interviews were audio recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed thematically. The study was reported following the COREQ checklist.
RESULTS: 21 participants were initially recruited with one participant withdrawing prior to the interview. Participants (n = 20) identified as predominantly female (n = 11) compared to male (n = 9) with a mean age of 62 years (range 36-82). Most participants were in surveillance stage (n = 16). Participants identified their level of digital literacy as competent (n = 14). However, 12 cited inadequate proficiency with digital technology requiring additional assistance. Two key themes reflected the procedural information needs throughout the cancer journey and factors that either eased or complicated the experience and were identified: Information and Digital Platform, each with corresponding subthemes.
CONCLUSION: Findings emphasise a hybrid system of information is advocated by CRC patients. The ability to access information varies and is dependent on personal preferences and stages of the cancer journey and via different information platforms. Whilst written and verbal information were preferred pathways, digital platforms offered others autonomy and accessibility to information when required.
